title: panic with SIGSEGV in kubeadm certs check-expiration
body:
### What happened?

```
$ kubeadm certs check-expiration 
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x18 pc=0x16c0556]

goroutine 1 [running]:
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal.fileExists({0xc000501360?, 0x1c1ab60?})
        cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal/readwriter.go:74 +0x56
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal.(*kubeConfigReadWriter).Exists(0x1c1ab60?)
        cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal/readwriter.go:124 +0x1e
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal.(*Manager).CertificateExists(0x21f6180?, {0x1f0b722, 0xa})
        cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/certs/renewal/manager.go:325 +0x4a
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd.newCmdCertsExpiration.func1(0xc0005c1400?, {0x3259d80?, 0x4?, 0x1f03ff0?})
        cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/certs.go:403 +0x234
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).execute(0xc000004600, {0x3259d80, 0x0, 0x0})
        vendor/github.com/spf13/cobra/command.go:940 +0x87c
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).ExecuteC(0xc00027d800)
        vendor/github.com/spf13/cobra/command.go:1068 +0x3a5
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).Execute(0x21f5ee0?)
        vendor/github.com/spf13/cobra/command.go:992 +0x13
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app.Run()
        cmd/kubeadm/app/kubeadm.go:50 +0x155
main.main()
        cmd/kubeadm/kubeadm.go:25 +0x13
$
```
When the command is run with superuser privileges, it prints the requested information.
### What did you expect to happen?

Print a warning that files could not be read due to insufficient permission, or that information was missing (e.g., when the /etc/kubernetes directory is not initialized).
When the directory is readable, it works as expected:
```
$ kubeadm certs check-expiration

!MISSING! ca

!MISSING! front-proxy-ca                             
$ 
```
where OS and kubeadm version detail was:
```
$ uname -a

$ cat /etc/os-release

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

title: NewVolumeManagerReconstruction: Volumes are reported as unmounted after reboot
body:
### What happened?

Kubernetes 1.27 with `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature gate **enabled** and `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` **disabled**, a rebooted node is not able to re-start pods that were running there before the reboot.

The node reports in Pod events:

```
Warning  FailedMount             2m4s (x5 over 11m)  kubelet                  Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[myvol], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The Pod should start just fine.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On Kubernetes 1.27:
1. Enable NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate.
2. Run a StatefulSet that uses a volume.
3. Force-reboot the node which runs the StatefulSet Pod.

### Anything else we need to know?

The reason is that kubelet's VolumeManager reconstructs the volume as _uncertain_ during startup and it uses a provisional _outer volume name_ for it, because it has not seen the API server and Pods in it yet. This provisional volume ID is then used in ActualStateOfWorld forever.

While kubelet _does_ mount the volume after reboot, it's not able to match it with the Pod that needs it. Kubelet reports `unmounted volumes=[myvol]`, while the volume is mounted with ID `pvc-6357c1ec-bac1-45fd-822f-2d6a014a9721` in my case (= the provisional name, we use PV.name for it) and not `myvol` (=`pod.spec.volumes[*].name`).

It is not reproducible with `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` enabled.

@lizhipeng629

well, I think this should be a point that can be improved. This sysctl is a host-level configuration, and we should avoid it affecting the entire host.

/cc @uablrek @aojea
IMO `kube-proxy` shouldn't tamper with sysctl at all, and never when it isn't ansolutely necessary. Someone may want the sysctl set for other reasons, and `kube-proxy` should not reset it.

When kube-proxy is in ipvs mode and using metallb as a load balancing service, it should be required to configure `strictARP`. see https://metallb.universe.tf/installation/#preparation.

If strictARP is set to false or kube-proxy mode switches to iptables mode, should we restore the sysctl? I think yes, since we no longer need to configure it and we don't want it to affect the rest of the host's progress.
You can't say "restore", since you don't know if it was `kube-proxy` that set it in the first place. It may be set by a user, e.g. in `/etc/sysctl.conf`, because they need it.

> You can't say "restore"

sorry for my bad words. I would say that if the user needs it then they would set `strictARP ` to true and then kube-proxy sets the sysctl. If the user still needs it, I don't think they would want to change `strictARP` to false?

If they really don't need it anymore, currently, they need to set the sysctl manually for each node, so it would be nice if we could set `strictARP` to false and then kube-proxy could help us set the sysctl.

Yes, this is precisely why the issue arose. I assumed that kube-proxy would revert any changes made upon setting it origin(default) value. Prior to reviewing the code, I was unaware of the things kube-proxy would do to my nodes under such circumstances. It seemed logical to me that it would undo any modifications to my nodes upon being set to false.

> > You can't say "restore"
> 
> sorry for my bad words. I would say that if the user needs it then they would set `strictARP ` to true and then kube-proxy sets the sysctl. If the user still needs it, I don't think they would want to change `strictARP` to false?
> 
> If they really don't need it anymore, currently, they need to set the sysctl manually for each node, so it would be nice if we could set `strictARP` to false and then kube-proxy could help us set the sysctl.

The kernel doc for reference:
```
arp_ignore - INTEGER
	Define different modes for sending replies in response to
	received ARP requests that resolve local target IP addresses:

	- 0 - (default): reply for any local target IP address, configured
	  on any interface
	- 1 - reply only if the target IP address is local address
	  configured on the incoming interface
	- 2 - reply only if the target IP address is local address
	  configured on the incoming interface and both with the
	  sender's IP address are part from same subnet on this interface
	- 3 - do not reply for local addresses configured with scope host,
	  only resolutions for global and link addresses are replied
	- 4-7 - reserved
	- 8 - do not reply for all local addresses

	The max value from conf/{all,interface}/arp_ignore is used
	when ARP request is received on the {interface}
```
When "strictARP" it true, `kube-proxy` ensures arp_ignore=1. In K8s this is AFAIK _only_ needed for proxy-mode=ipvs _and_ MetalLB in `L2 mode`.

For other reasons the cluster admin may however _want_ `arp_ignore != 0` (not necessarily 1) and explicitly configure it on node start-up. `Kube-proxy` MUST NOT force it to `0`!

`StrictARP=true` is never _required_ for `kube-proxy` in iptables or nftables mode (even though the cluster admin may want `arp_ignore != 0` for other reasons, as mentioned). So, I propose that `strictARP` is deprecated and obsoleted when the nftables mode becomes default.

> For other reasons the cluster admin may however want arp_ignore != 0 (not necessarily 1) and explicitly configure it on node start-up. Kube-proxy MUST NOT force it to 0!


this logic not make sense. see below: 
"also  Kube-proxy MUST NOT force it to !0  if cluster admin set it to 0"

>  "also Kube-proxy MUST NOT force it to !0 if cluster admin set it to 0"

I agree. That's why kube-proxy, or K8s in general should not [tamper with the sysctls](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123992#issuecomment-2011330857). But for historic and backward compatibility reasons, we must.

/assign @uablrek 
/cc @aojea

This was discussed today during sig network meeting, an important context is that we have a debt we need to deal with that is setting sysctl and that we are trying to avoid keep doing it.

We have now an option in kube-proxy IPVS that says 

> strictARP configures arp_ignore and arp_announce to avoid answering ARP queries from kube-ipvs0 interface

this effectively means that if strictARP:
- is false, it does not do anything
- is true kube-proxy set `net/ipv4/conf/all/arp_ignore` to 1 and `net/ipv4/conf/all/arp_announce` to 2

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f4e246bc93ffb68b33ed67c7896c379efa4207e7/pkg/proxy/ipvs/proxier.go#L325-L335

The request seems to be to give meaning to strictARP equal false to mean set `net/ipv4/conf/all/arp_ignore` to 0 and `net/ipv4/conf/all/arp_announce` to 0

The reason we can not do this is because as Lars says, if we make false to set some specific values, we'll always been overriding the sysctl config, since this option is a bool there is no way to differentiate if the user is indicating that it wants to `restore strictARP`  values or just is using the default value that means "leave the sysctl as they are"


https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f4e246bc93ffb68b33ed67c7896c379efa4207e7/pkg/proxy/apis/config/types.go#L70-L72


/close

Whilst we're likely to work on this issue and spend at least some time looking into what'd help towards a fix, I'm not sure that Kubernetes + containerd + Debian is a _supported_ combination.

So far as I know, we - Kubernetes - don't publish a matrix of combinations of operating system, container runtime, network plugin, OCI-level runtime, Kubernetes version, CPU architecture showing which of those are officially supported. title: SecretProviderClass should be versioned similar to configmaps
body:
### What happened?

Let's say we have a service A, which currently depends on 2 secrets, B & C, provided by a `SecretProviderClass`.

Then, a new version of A removed the usage of secret C, so it now only need one secret B.

When deploying the new version, 2 things will happen:

1. The `SecretProviderClass` being updated to remove C and only provide B
2. The pods for A being _gradually_ replaced by the new version that no longer needs C

But since 1 is almost immediate while 2 is always a gradual rollout, after 1 is replaced the old pods still requiring both B and C will likely start to fail because the update of `SecretProviderClass` that removed C that they still require.

Even if we tweak the order to only do 1 after 2 is fully done, it can still cause the reverse problem (a new version that requires a new secret).

Currently, to avoid this issue we need to be extra careful and do 2-step deploys, first deploy a superset of `SecretProviderClass` that contains the secrets for both new and old version of code with the new code, and after that's fully done, do another deploy to shrink `SecretProviderClass` to only the ones needed by the new version.

But I think to fully address this problem, we should make `SecretProviderClass` versioned (similar to how configmaps are versioned), so every pod can use their matching version of `SecretProviderClass` to provide the secrets they need.

title: Issues with runtime handler supported feature lookup
body:
There were a couple changes to merged in v1.30 to guard user namespaces & recursive read only mounts based on runtime self-reported support. When looking through the code, I noticed the following issues:

1. Lookup is done by `runtimeClassName`, rather than `runtimeHandler`:
    - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2453
    - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/util/util.go#L104-L107
    - Should be using `LookupRuntimeHandler` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/runtimeclass/runtimeclass_manager.go#L61
2. Version skew is not handled in the case where the container runtime doesn't provide any RuntimeHandlers, which results in a lot of log spam:
    ```
    Mar 12 19:17:29 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:29.342999     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    Mar 12 19:17:29 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:29.347115     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""

title: Pods are incorrectly rejected after kubelet restart due to NUMA and node label changes
body:
### What happened?

1.NUMA causing rejection:
Node configuration: --cpu-manager-policy=static --memory-manager-policy=Static --topology-manager-policy=single-numa-node
InitContainer and main container's NUMA are calculated one by one.
CPU affinity is present, but in reality, the NUMA alignment of the InitContainer might not match the resource requirements of the main container.
Restarting kubelet leads to Pod rejection.
![WX20240311-175733@2x](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/46776140/4ca5624f-3caa-4ba3-9518-6fb5148fe376)

2.Node Label change causing rejection:
Node has a label hpc=true, and the Pod has nodeAffinity based on this label.
Due to specific reasons, the label is removed.
Restarting kubelet results in Pod rejection with the error message: NodeAffinity failed

### What did you expect to happen?

Regardless of the situation, kubelet should not reject Pods that are running and were created before the kubelet restart.

> Does this happen with a kubelet restart (just the kubelet) or with a full node reboot?

Yes, but it's quite cumbersome,  it can be reproduce by:
1. Node has N NUMA, every NUMA has 40 Core CPU
2. Pod A created with 1 Core init-container, and 40 Core app container, and it can use all NUMA 0.
3. Pod B created with 2 Core, because of NUMA 0 CPU is fully used by Pod A, Pod B got CPU in NUMA 1.
4. Delete Pod A
5. ReCreate Pod A, so Pod A's created timestamp is greater than Pod B. Pod A still use NUMA 0.
6. Delete checkpoint
7. Restart Kubelet

After restart kubelet, kubelet will admit all Pods in node, sort by createdTime https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b3926d137cd2964cd3a04088ded30845910547b1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2539.
1. Pod B is allocate first, so it get 2 Core in  NUMA 0.
2. Then Pod A init-container, it get 1 Core in NUMA 0.
3. Pod A app-container will failed (NUMA 0 CPU not enough; NUMA 1 or other NUMA node is passed because of reuse CPU)

> moving to point 2 above, it would be nice to learn why the node label changes. I wouldn't expect to node labels to be dropped across kubelet restarts (or node reboots) without explicit action like explicit delete.

The reason why this label changed is because the operation and maintenance engineer organized the node label, such as hpc=true, and removed this label. When a pod is compatible with this label, restarting the node kubelet will cause the pod to be rebuilt. This actually shouldn’t be the case. It will affect the normal operation of the business.

> part 1 is a duplicate of #123816. Please file a separate bug for part 2

In fact, the problem I want to solve when raising this PR is that no matter what the circumstances, pods that are running normally should not be rejected. Different problem than #123816 wants to solve.

> > moving to point 2 above, it would be nice to learn why the node label changes. I wouldn't expect to node labels to be dropped across kubelet restarts (or node reboots) without explicit action like explicit delete.
> 
> The reason why this label changed is because the operation and maintenance engineer organized the node label, such as hpc=true, and removed this label. When a pod is compatible with this label, restarting the node kubelet will cause the pod to be rebuilt. This actually shouldn’t be the case. It will affect the normal operation of the business.

The thing is, pod assignment is not sticky. Meaning. Once a scheduler decided which node should run a pod, this decision is not kept forever, and when a new scheduling attempt is done for whatever reason, the cluster state is re-evaluated.
A kubelet restart does the same: admission is re-attempted when kubelet restarts and it re-evaluates the pods which should be running on a node (as stored in the cluster state), and some conditions may cause admission failure.

That said, it's also true that despite this general condition, there's clearly an emerging consensus/sentiment about the fact that a kubelet restart should not affect the running workload. We "recently" discussed a [similar case](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118635).

So the case is here, but we need a separate issue and quite likely we will need also a larger scope conversation at SIG level and to move the topic to a different issue

> > part 1 is a duplicate of #123816. Please file a separate bug for part 2
> 
> In fact, the problem I want to solve when raising this PR is that no matter what the circumstances, pods that are running normally should not be rejected. Different problem than #123816 wants to solve.

OK, this is a fair point but we will need a refocusing of the issue. Filing a new issue about the general ask that restarting a kubelet should not cause any disruption to the running workload (which likely will mean skip admission of running pods, but let's not run ahead of ourselves) and backlink to this issue is probably the best way forward still.

Is much likely better to raise the most general issue ("restarting a kubelet should never affect the running workload") and then link specific examples than start with examples and then generalize.

title: StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration does not support ES256 algorithm
body:
### What happened?

I'm using [Pinniped](https://pinniped.dev/docs/background/architecture/) as an OIDC provider to authenticate users. following the Pinniped documentation we need to add the following flags to the api-server to trust supervisor as OICD provider
```
# Make this exactly match the spec.issuer of your Supervisor's FederationDomain.
# Note: It seems like the kube-apiserver pod cannot resolve `cluster.local`
# DNS names, so don't use one of those DNS names as the issuer.
--oidc-issuer-url="https://my-supervisor.example.com/my-issuer"

# This is only required if the kube-apiserver pod is not going to trust your
# Supervisor's FederationDomain's TLS certificates, e.g. if you used a
# self-signed CA. Make this match where you mounted the CA PEM file into
# your control plane node's filesystem, which must be under a directory
# that the kube-apiserver container is going to volume mount.
--oidc-ca-file="/etc/ca-certificates/supervisor/root-ca.pem"

# Choose a unique value for each cluster here. By making this unique, the
# Supervisor will be able to issue ID tokens for this cluster that cannot
# be used on any other cluster, which improves security. Do not use the
# special value "pinniped-cli" or any value that contains the substring
# ".pinniped.dev", because these special values are reserved for other
# purposes.
--oidc-client-id="my-cluster-342klb7h"

# Use these exact values. These are based on how the Supervisor issues ID
# tokens. Do not change these values.
--oidc-signing-algs="ES256"
--oidc-username-claim="username"
--oidc-groups-claim="groups"
```
which works fine. However when I tried to implement the same thing using the new featureGates `StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration ` in the apiserver as follow
```
- --feature-gates=StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration=true
- --authentication-config=/etc/kubernetes/auth-config.yaml
```

The output of `auth-config.yaml`
```
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: AuthenticationConfiguration
jwt:
  - issuer:
      url: https://my-supervisor.example.com/my-issuer

```

I'm getting ```Unable to authenticate the request err=[invalid bearer token, oidc; verify token: oidc: id token signed with unsupported algortithm, expected [\"RSA256\"] got \"ES256\"]"```

According to the quote from the KEP, all asymmetric algorithms are allowed, which is not the case
```
Goals:
Easy migration from existing OIDC flags
Note: we intend to drop the --oidc-signing-algs flag because this configuration provides no benefit (we will always allow all asymmetric algorithms)
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3331-structured-authentication-configuration#goals

ES256 is an asymmetric algorithm so it should be allowed

Allow all asymmetric algorithm

@HamzaZo looks like then intention is there `"oidc-signing-algs"` but the flag has NOT been deprecated yet. wanna try to specify that too?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authentication.go#L351-L354

@dims You mean that I need to add `- --oidc-signing-algs="ES256"` in the apiserver ?
```
- --feature-gates=StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration=true
- --authentication-config=/etc/kubernetes/auth-config.yaml

```
Even though the official documentation says 
```
Note: When the feature is enabled, setting both --authentication-config and any of the --oidc-* flags will result in an error. If you want to use the feature, you have to remove the --oidc-* flags and use the configuration file instead.
```
yes, please try that to see what happens.

We were running into the same problem, and we tried the `--oidc-signing-algs="ES256"` workaround.
Unfortunately the apiserver complains that `oidc-*` flags (including `oidc-signing-algs`)  are mutually exclusive with `authentication-config`.

Relevant code is here, I think. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.2/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authentication.go#L680

There is a bug present in version v1.29, which has been resolved through the patch provided in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123282. This fix will be included in the upcoming v1.30 release.

FYI `StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration` will be beta in `v1.30` and enabled by default.

@aramase my use case is to define two `oidc-client-id` using `StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration` (currently, using multiple --oidc-client-id flags is not supported in the api-server) Is there any workaround to implement without waiting for v1.30 ?

Multiple audience support in Authentication Configuration was only added in v1.30: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123165. There is no way to define more than one audience in authentication configuration in v1.29 or using the `oidc-*` flags. 

The recommendation would be to use the feature in `v1.30` that supports configuring multiple audiences, multiple JWT authenticators and contains the signing algs [fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123282).

Closing the issue with the above comment. Please try out the feature in `v1.30` and let us know your feedback.

### What happened?

1. Used the [ingress-nginx](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx) helm chart to deploy a dual stack ingress.

title: SetFeatureGateDuringTest doesn't work if test is run in pararell.
body:
### What happened?

`defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, true)()` should change the feature flag to true, however feature flag is a global state, so if somewhere in the test we call `t.Parallel()` there is a risk that some other test changes the flag state in the mean time.

Found this when we launched broken ConsistentListFromCache to Alpha and only noticed issues in Beta as the test didn't really test anything. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123674/files#r1511492942.



### What did you expect to happen?

We should protect against usage of `featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest` and `t.Parallel` in a single test. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
func TestFeatureGateOn(t *testing.T) {
	defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, true)()
	runFeatureGateTest(t, true)
}

func TestFeatureGateOff(t *testing.T) {
	defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, false)()
	runFeatureGateTest(t, false)
}

func runFeatureGateTest(t *testing.T, expectEnabled bool) {
	t.Parallel()
	time.Sleep(time.Second)
	gotEnabled := utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate.Enabled(features.ConsistentListFromCache)
	if gotEnabled != expectEnabled {
		t.Errorf("unexpected feature gate state, got: %v, want: %v", gotEnabled, expectEnabled)
	}
}
```

the alternative would be to get rid of the global state but that seems unfeasible as we would have to pass a feature gate implementation to every method that wants to use it.

title: [kubeadam][structured authz] can't use structured authz due to default `--authorization-mode` flag
body:
### What happened? **TL;DR** https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L232 prevents us from using structured authz (setting `--authorization-config` flag) as those flags are mutually exclusive /cc @palnabarun (as the author of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120154) /cc @liggitt FYI @stealthybox @robscott To use structured authz you need to define the authorization configuration using the `--authorization-config` flag. However this flag is mutually exclusive with `--authorization-modes` and `--authorization-webhook-*` flags. (refer to [1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authorization.go#L113) & [2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authorization/#configuring-the-api-server-using-an-authorization-config-file)) Kubeadam adds `--authorization-mode` by default ([1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L232) & [2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L241)) which prevents us from using `--authorization-config` ### What did you expect to happen? I should be able to define the `authorization-config` flag and have structured authz working. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? Spin up a kind cluster using this kind config (make sure the images are > 1.29 for structured authz to be avaliable) ```yaml kind: Cluster apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4 featureGates: StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration: true kubeadmConfigPatches: - | kind: ClusterConfiguration metadata: name: config apiServer: extraArgs: authorization-config: "/files/authorization_config.yaml" extraVolumes: - name: api-server-basic-auth-files hostPath: "/files" mountPath: "/files" readOnly: true nodes: - role: control-plane # add a mount from /path/to/my/files on the host to /files on the node extraMounts: - hostPath: /refgrant-poc/files containerPath: /files ``` (For this bug, the content of `/files/authorization_config.yaml` doesn't matter.) However, the cluster become unhealthy. docker exec to the kind cluster container, where we can see the inner container of the apiserver has exited. Running `crictl logs ` we can see this error ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
```console The kind cluster version image: `kindest/node:v1.29.2` ```

title: Multiple Timestamp Directories Exist in the Mount Directory After the Server Is Powered Off
body:
### What happened?

Background: I have a K8S cluster, version is v1.25.3, on the master node core1 there is a deployment mounted secret (named ssl). In normal cases, the mount directory in the container is as follows:
![正常挂载](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/d4f7c38a-e1ac-40bb-b67a-3df5a119498e)
![挂载目录](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/181387d8-f08f-4782-929e-fa26ff3a6685)
But when I reboot the machine and go to the container to view the mount directory, it looks like this:
![reboot后](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/4d885d9b-fba6-4892-a090-aa55f2d506ad)
A timestamp directory is generated upon each reboot. The permission of the files in the directory that is not linked by the soft link..data can be changed. In the preceding figure, the permission is changed to 700.
![多次reboot](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/1cbd218e-192e-4b4c-b8bd-4679f450bf28)
When I restarted the pod, the mount directory was back to normal.
![重弹](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/73e539c1-c9cd-486c-92c3-1407c527d8af)
While restarting the pod will make this go away, I want to keep only one mounted timestamp directory. If the timestamp directory is not linked by ..data, the permission can be changed. For example, in the preceding figure, the permission is changed to 700 because of this container’s command. If sensitive files exist in the timestamp directory and the permission is too high, the files are insecure for enterprises. In addition, power-off is inevitable.
![配置](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/81507e7a-5077-40f3-b79f-02dd62c6f68b)
Therefore, I think that there should be only one timestamp directory in the power-off scenario. There should not be a timestamp directory whose permissions can be changed and that contains sensitive files when mounting secrets.


### What did you expect to happen?

Only One Timestamp Directory Exists in the Mount Directory After the Linux Machine Is Powered Off

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Mount the projection data volume to the container and reboot the linux machine.

### Anything else we need to know?

I added the log in atomic_write.go and then I rebooted the linux machine. By looking at the kubelet logs, I know that the reason the old timestamp directory wasn't deleted was because it didn't successfully get the directory pointed to by ..data.

I add the log in the code like this：
![代码](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/66065665/a94a8541-400d-4ca1-8032-6db6a58bc683)
After the machine is rebooted, there is a log like this:
```
-------dataDirPath is /var/lib/kubelet/pods/01352a44-7d9e-445d-940f-7653118abc8c/volumes/kubernetes.iowsecret/ssl/..data ------
-------oldTsDir is  -------
-------oldTsPath is /var/lib/kubelet/pods/01352a44-7d9e-445d-940f-7653118abc8c/volumes/kubernetes.iowsecret/ssl -------
```
After the code  `oldTsDir, err := os.Readlink(dataDirPath)`  is executed, the value of variable `oldTsDir` is empty.

title: In a time leap scenario, it may render the service account token unavailable.
body:
### What happened?

Starting from Kubernetes version 1.21, Service Account Tokens are obtained through the TokenRequest API to acquire a JWT token with a specific expiration time. If the token's validity exceeds 24 hours or 80% of ExpirationSeconds, kubelet will proactively refresh the token.

In a time leap scenario, if the system time is adjusted to a time beyond the token's expiration, kubelet will refresh the token automatically, ensuring no issues arise. However, if the system time is set to a time before the token's validity period, kubelet will not automatically update the token, leading to a 401 error when containers attempt to access the API server.

### What did you expect to happen?

If the system time is adjusted to a time before or after the token's validity period, kubelet will proactively refresh the token for the pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. View service account token details:
    `cat /var/lib/kubelet/pods/{pod uid}/volumes/kubernetes.io~projected/kube-api-access-xxxx/token`
2. Parse the JWT token, check the "iat" field, and then adjust the system time to be earlier than that time.

3. Subsequently, you will notice a large number of client 401 errors in the kube-apiserver logs:

    E0220 00:01:07.525160       1 authentication.go:63] "Unable to authenticate the request" err="[invalid bearer token, service account token is not valid yet]"
    I0220 00:01:07.525322       1 httplog.go:131] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/api" latency="856.07µs" userAgent="test/v0.0.0 (linux/arm64) kubernetes/$Format/test" audit--
    ID="f8a8a29a-6f95-427d-b467-e4997d29aa25" srcIP="172.16.0.133:47038" resp=401


### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"25+", GitVersion:"v1.25.3-h0.dsiv.test.r3-dirty", GitCommit:"308d9d6535243cebbce78461f486b6f42b6d24d9", GitTreeState:"dirty", BuildDate:"2024-02-06T02:23:07Z", GoVersion:"go1.19.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/arm64"}

However, if the system time is set to a time before the token's validity period, kubelet will not automatically update the token, leading to a 401 error when containers attempt to access the API server.

this seems like something that can be improved.
SIG auth can provide feedback.

but FWIW, time leap can break a lot of things and is generally not advisable.
the kubelet automatic client cert rotation comes to mind. we (at kubeadm) continue to occasionally get reports where the kubelet client cert did not renew "on time".

I submitted a PR.

title: Parallel pod deletion makes kubectl stuck forever
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl delete pod` may become stuck during execution of the following steps:
* Restart kubelet `systemctl restart kubelet`
* Force remove all containers for static pods `crictl ps --name '(kube-apiserver|kube-scheduler|kube-controller-manager|etcd)' -q | xargs -I CONTAINER sudo crictl rm -f CONTAINER`
* Try to delete some static pod `kubectl delete pod -n kube-system kube-controller-manager-k8s-control-plane-1`

Result: kubectl prints that the pod is deleted, but never exits.

It seems that the problem is caused by parallel deletion of the pod by kubelet.
Please see details in the steps to reproduce.


### What did you expect to happen?

kubectl exits.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install single-node cluster
2. Run script
<details>

```sh
#!/bin/bash

for i in {1..100} ; do
  echo "Attempt $i"
  systemctl restart kubelet
  crictl ps --name '(kube-apiserver|kube-scheduler|kube-controller-manager|etcd)' -q | xargs -I CONTAINER sudo crictl rm -f CONTAINER
  for component in kube-apiserver kube-scheduler kube-controller-manager etcd; do
    while true ; do
      echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S,%N') delete $component"
      if kubectl --v=10 delete pod -n kube-system ${component}-k8s-control-plane-1 2> failed.txt ; then
        break
      fi
    done
  done
  for component in kube-apiserver kube-scheduler kube-controller-manager etcd; do
    while true ; do
      echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S,%N') get $component"
      if kubectl get pod -n kube-system ${component}-k8s-control-plane-1 | grep '1/1' ; then
        break
      fi
      sleep 5
    done
  done
done
```
</details>

Regarding part 1, I think audit logs containing sensitive information might be WAI? In case of security intrusion, this can help understand what changes a bad actor made.

`kube-apiserver` takes the `--audit-policy-file` flag to control how much you want to log. You can use the following policy to avoid logging the full request header.

```
- level: Metadata
  resources:
  - group: "" 
    resources: ["secrets", "serviceaccounts/token"]
  - group: authentication.k8s.io
    resources: ["tokenreviews"]
  omitStages:

title: Readiness probe success during preStop hook causes replicas scaling
body:
### What happened?

We are using Readiness and liveness probes in the deployment while `preStop` hook is set to `sleep 60` in order to gracefully shutdown pods.

When we update a deployment by setting a new image, a new Pod is created.  Due to slow start of the JVM, it accidentally failed all initial Readiness and liveness probes attempts. Then the preStop hook is called and the pod is scheduled to be killed after a period of time (for example 60 seconds in our case).

According to the current design, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122824#issuecomment-1896099927, the Readiness probe will not be stopped. And in some cases, we've observed the Readiness probe passed and the new RS was scaled up while the old RS was scaled down.

But this Pod will be terminated after 60 seconds. So after some time, no Pod is healthy.

### What did you expect to happen?

The Readiness probe does not lead to the reconcile of deployment-controller.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The timeline is designed as following,

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/2568208/65a55d67-a169-48ec-a5c3-778be0771350)

Any readiness probe attempt pass within the orange zone will cause this issue.

First, we can start a Kubernetes version `1.22` with kind,

```yaml
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
  image: kindest/node:v1.22.17@sha256:f5b2e5698c6c9d6d0adc419c0deae21a425c07d81bbf3b6a6834042f25d4fba2
```

Then write a simple Go application to control when the probes can pass,

```go
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

var (
	_                      http.Handler = (*healthHandler)(nil)
	startTime                           = time.Now()
	healthThresholdSeconds int
)

type healthHandler struct{}

func (h healthHandler) ServeHTTP(writer http.ResponseWriter, request *http.Request) {
	if time.Now().Sub(startTime).Seconds() > float64(healthThresholdSeconds) {
		writer.WriteHeader(200)
		writer.Write([]byte("ok"))
		return
	}
	writer.WriteHeader(500)
	writer.Write([]byte("not healthy"))
}

func main() {
	flag.IntVar(&healthThresholdSeconds, "health-threshold-seconds", 30, "delay")
	flag.Parse()
	log.Println(fmt.Sprintf("health probe will start after %d seconds", healthThresholdSeconds))
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", &healthHandler{}))
}
```

Then deploy this application to the cluster,

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 2
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 0
    type: RollingUpdate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: webapp
          image: kubernetes-prober:latest
          resources:
            limits:
              memory: "64Mi"
              cpu: "10m"
          args:
            - -health-threshold-seconds=55
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command:
                  - sleep
                  - "30"
          livenessProbe:
            failureThreshold: 3
            httpGet:
              path: /check
              port: 8080
              scheme: HTTP
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
            successThreshold: 1
            timeoutSeconds: 5
          readinessProbe:
            failureThreshold: 3
            httpGet:
              path: /check
              port: 8080
              scheme: HTTP
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
            successThreshold: 1
            timeoutSeconds: 5
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Startup Probe does help in this scenario if we patch the deployment above,

```yaml
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /check
              port: 8080
            failureThreshold: 60
            periodSeconds: 5
```

1.27.x also suffers from this issue,

```yaml
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
  image: kindest/node:v1.22.17@sha256:f5b2e5698c6c9d6d0adc419c0deae21a425c07d81bbf3b6a6834042f25d4fba2
```

$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.1
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.22.17
WARNING: version difference between client (1.29) and server (1.22) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1
```

# paste output here

C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture

```

Is this behavior considered part of Kubernetes' designed behavior for managing pod lifecycle events and deployment updates, or is it an unintended consequence that needs addressing?

title: sidecar container readniess result to be used in Pod ready state also for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Never or OnFailure
body:
### What happened?

I created a pod with sidecar container with following manifest:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: simple-webapp
  labels:
    app: webapp
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "key1"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  initContainers:
    - name: init-service
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 5s
    - name: sidecar
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 30s
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-logs
          mountPath: /var/log/nginx
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
          - cat
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 5
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main-application
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
      - name: shared-logs
        mountPath: /var/log/nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "100Mi"
        cpu: "0.5"
  volumes:
    - name: shared-logs
      emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never

```

watch the pod readiness. 
```
#before the sidecar container be restarted , the readiness is 2/2
watch kubectl  get pod
Every 2.0s: kubectl get pod                                                     

NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           2/2     Running   0          36s

#after the sidecar container be restarted, the pod readiness is 1/2, sidecar readiness result is not be used to the pod. 
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           1/2     Running   2          2m15s

```
in [Sidecar containers and Pod lifecycle](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/#sidecar-containers-and-pod-lifecycle), it's mentioned "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod."

it's true only for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Always, sidecar container readniess result will be used in Pod ready state, neither "Never" or "OnFailure".

I tested with v1.29.0

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod." also applicable to  pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Set pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console

title: OpenAPI handler fails on duplicated path
body:
### What happened?

When installing the metrics-server to implement the metrics.k8s.io API and the prometheus-adapter to implement the custom.metrics.k8s.io API, it is possible to make the OpenAPI handler fail to initialize with this error log in apiserver: https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/blob/master/pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go#L343
```
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/pods
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/{namespace}/pods
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes/{name}
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
```
This will result in kubectl discovery calls to /openapi/v2 to fail with a 503:
```
{
  "kind": "Event",
  "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",
  "level": "Metadata",

  "stage": "ResponseComplete",
  "requestURI": "/openapi/v2?timeout=31s",

...

    "authorization.k8s.io/decision": "allow",

}
```


### What did you expect to happen?

The OpenAPI handler should not fail to initialize if both metrics.k8s.io and custom.metrics.k8s.io are serving the same path for different API groups/versions.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I can provide exact installation steps if needed, however, a high-level repro is:
- install metrics-server to serve v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io  
- install prometheus-adapter to serve v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io
- ensure resourceRules is populated in the prometheus-adapter config so that resource metrics are also served by v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/prometheus-adapter/blob/7a421bb91e9ea52be4e26db22392c36c8af38bc8/deploy/manifests/custom-metrics-config-map.yaml#L73-L98

@Jefftree the prometheus-adapter can also be configured to serve metrics.k8s.io and replace the metrics-server by enabling these metrics, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/prometheus-adapter/blob/7a421bb91e9ea52be4e26db22392c36c8af38bc8/deploy/manifests/custom-metrics-config-map.yaml#L73-L98. 

However, if the prometheus-adapter fronts custom.metrics.k8s.io and metrics-server fronts metrics.k8s.io, it does seem like the correct behavior would be for prometheus-adapter to serve /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes until an operator updates the metrics.k8s.io APIService to reference prometheus-adapter rather than metrics-server. We're seeing this issue occur for upgrades between 1.27 and 1.28 so it does look this path duplication did not cause the OpenAPI handler to fail on 1.27.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This is an interesting issue that came up from a bug report. Currently, OpenAPI v2 is downloaded and merged from aggregated apiservices in its entirety, filtering for only `/apis/*` endpoints. As a result, any aggregated apiservice can claim they serve another endpoint and will be included in the resulting openapi. This is not usually a problem with overriding built-ins because we have different priorities. However, between apiservices gv priorities are usually the same, and merge order is not as deterministic. Thus, a malicious apiservice may claim they serve something like `/apis/someothergroup/version` despite their gv registered as `/apis/stable.example.com/v1`. This PR fixes that such that only the OpenAPI for an apiservice's registered GV is merged and published.

There is an orthogonal bug in [kube-openapi's merging](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/blame/master/pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go#L73-L75)  but that will be addressed separately.

We identified an edge case here with Kubernetes v1.29.

If a cloud provider did not yet initialise the node's `.status.addresses`, the code for creating the `/etc/hosts` file including the hostAliases does not get run.

To be concrete, in:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3f7a50f38688eb332e2a1b013678c6435d539ae6/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L160

`podIPs` is empty in this case which leads to `mountEtcHostsFile` to be `false`.

I was able to trace it back to this change which leads to this behaviour for static pods:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121028

For confirmation: I reverted the above commit, rebuilt kubelet and it got back to the old behaviour.

> For confirmation: I reverted the above commit, rebuilt kubelet and it got back to the old behaviour.

> This behavior has undesired consequences if the cloud-provider addresses are different than the original ones, specially for hostNetwork pods, that inherit these addresses from the Node.

> Since some cloud-providers depend on this behavior, in order to keep backward compatibility, assume that the specifying addresses via the node-ip flags means that the intent is to keep the existing behavior to temporary initialize the addresses.

there is no perfect solution, but reverting is wrong because opens another bug, we need to study this more carefully but in the meantime installers that know the nodes addresses beforehand should set the --node-ip flag or not use cloud-provider external

yeah, as i mentioned downstream, revering https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121028 is out of the question. it fixes some long standing problems.

nodes.body: related PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122320
/sig network

This similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120937 ,  the nodeport value is an int32, so there is no way to differentiate between an empty value or someone explicitly setting the nodeport to 0

```
k patch svc rest-1 -p '{"spec":{"$setElementOrder/ports":[{"port":8080}],"ports":[{"nodePort":0,"port":8080}]}}'
```

is the same as, isn't it?
```
k patch svc rest-1 -p '{"spec":{"$setElementOrder/ports":[{"port":8080}],"ports":[{"port":8080}]}}'
```

the result is same because the default value of int32 in golang is 0. the struct label is omitempty. the 0 is default value and not shown.

i applied the patch in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122320 and the update succeeds to remove the nodePort value. the corresponding port listening in nodes is cleaned, too.
That's the point, if an user does not specify the nodeport in a patch with your PR, it will get the nodeports removed, that is not what it wants

that's a valid concern that the NodePort's value is a system managed field. the original value is not provided by the raw specs. so another `kubectl apply -f xxx.service.yaml` can prune the NodePort values unexpectedly. 

then the NodePort values need to be a subresource to guarantee isolated writes from system controllers, as well as updates on purpose. 
or give it a negative value or out of range value as the option to tell it's an on purpose NodePort deletion.

now the precreate validation blocks negative values, and reset the value to the original value if the original value is still valid, if the NodePort is set to 0, by deletion or set to 0.

for subresource option, it's likely the right way to make it. and it takes also more efforts on the registry store:
* add /nodeport subresource
* implement OnUpdate hook to allow updating NodePort values
* corresponding UTs/E2Es

a Int32.MaxValue option seems a easier way comparing with subresource. but hard to understand, also hard to remember.
a negative value solution works in the similar as int32.MaxValue. I prefer to call it a workaround.

i prefer the subresource way . @aojea  how do you think about it and what solutions do you propose?

title: plugins that register nodeAdd in EventsToRegister must register nodeUpdate
body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

Plugins may miss Node-related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

So, no matter whether plugins have QueueingHint or not, plugins must register NodeUpdate event when they're interested in NodeAdd. Also, in case they have QHint, they should take this scenario into consideration.

Yes i can reproduce this one and provide kubelet logs

> Now, any idea what the correct behavior should be? For kubelet, `NodeUnstage` has finished...

Not an expert here but maybe we should not issue NodeStage/Publish and make the volume uncertain/Not Ready if the volume is currently going through the NodeUnstage RPC.

> maybe we should not issue NodeStage/Publish and make the volume uncertain/Not Ready if the volume is currently going through the NodeUnstage RPC.

How kubelet knows there is NodeUnstage in progress? From kubelet point of view, the gRPC call finished with `DeadlineExceeded`. It cannot wait forever.

CSI spec says that [cancelling a call](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/blob/master/spec.md#timeouts) with "negation" is allowed and that's what kubelet does here. Of course, CSI driver can return some reasonable NodeStage errors until NodeUnstage completes and the driver can really start with NodeStage.

I'm open to suggestions to make driver's life easier, but there are not so many options in gRPC.

body:
Expression `factor`

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/11902a838028edef305dfe2f96be929bc4d114d8/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/values.go#L208

used as **divisor** at 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/11902a838028edef305dfe2f96be929bc4d114d8/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/values.go#L203-L213

may have **a zero value** when variable `factor` has value `0`. 

Check at 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/11902a838028edef305dfe2f96be929bc4d114d8/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/values.go#L205-L207

_does not prevent this error_.

Here we get a **DIVISION_BY_ZERO**.

P.S. This problem is relevant for the _branch 1.26_ 

Found by Linux Verification Center ([portal.linuxtesting.ru](https://portal.linuxtesting.ru/)) with SVACE.

Author E. Bykhanova.

title: Possible data race in code
body:
### What happened?

In file: [evented.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L171C23-L171C41), there is a possible data race in `watchEventsChannel` while accessing `eventedPLEGUsage`. 

In line [176](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L176), there is a goroutine invocation. Inside the goroutine, in line [183](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L183), there is a call to `e.Stop()`. Inside that function's implementation, there is an invocation of function `setEventedPLEGUsage` in line [134](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L134). Inside that method, in line [59](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L59), the value of  `eventedPLEGUsage` is written.

However, in line [201](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L201), this value is accessed in a readonly manner when the function `isEventedPLEGInUse` is called which reads `eventedPLEGUsage`.

Even though inside the function  `isEventedPLEGInUse` and `setEventedPLEGUsage` , the [read](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L48) and [write](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L56) accesses to `eventedPLEGUsage` are guarded by locks, the global order of these function invocations are non-deterministic. In one interval, `isEventedPLEGInUse` in the main routine may be called before the other; in another interval, this may happen the other way. 


### What did you expect to happen?

This is not reported by a run time observation. This is reported by a static analysis tool.

title: In case of node reboot, pod running on that node goes to "Unknown" state, as kubelet fails to attach the PVC associated
body:
### What happened?

Given a Kubernetes cluster with Windows worker nodes and a vSphere CSI driver installed, when a worker node is rebooted, pod, running on the restarting node, goes to "Unknown" state from a "Running" state, and remains in same "Unknown" state forever.
The error seen in corresponding pod description for both of the above cases is as shown below:

```
  Warning  FailedMount  9m11s (x2131 over 3d)  kubelet  MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "pvc-X-X-X-X-X" : kubernetes.io/csi: attacher.MountDevice failed to create dir "\\var\\lib\\kubelet\\plugins\\kubernetes.io\\csi\\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\\XXXXX\\globalmount":  mkdir \var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\XXXXX\globalmount: Cannot create a file when that file already exists.
  Warning  FailedMount  3m42s (x1495 over 3d)  kubelet  Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[<abc>], unattached volumes=[<abc> kube-api-access-8dqhl]: timed out waiting for the condition
```

If the pod in this state is deleted forcefully and gets rescheduled on same node, it does not enter "Running" state but remains in "ContainerCreating" state forever with same error in pod description as above case.

The error above states that during `MountDevice()` in `csi_attacher.go`, kubelet fails to create staging target path directory as the directory already exists.

Before the change done by PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88759, kubelet was checking if staging target directory is present and mounted already, but the check was removed considering that mount point related checks should be done at CSI driver level, not generally at kubelet level. 

However, in cases of node shutdown/reboot, unmount and removal of the staging target path directory may not be possible or may fail for various reasons, which would leave the staging directory created on that node as it is. So, when the pod gets re-scheduled on that same node, and kubelet tries to create the directory again, it fails at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8b90c9008609913c3b9b8f5b146e68d9ec8146f/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L342.

Similar code exists in `SetUpAt()` in `csi_mounter.go` ( https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8b90c9008609913c3b9b8f5b146e68d9ec8146f/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L211 ), that can also lead to same issue before NodePublishVolume().

The issue was seen originally in context of Windows worker node. However, the kubelet code is common regardless of OS flavors. Thus, the issue can be seen in case of Linux worker node as well.

### What did you expect to happen?

kubelet should handle node reboot/restart like cases, where the staging target path directory for the PVC can be already present on the node and let the corresponding CSI driver handle the further processing on that target directory in `NodeStageVolume()` and `NodePublishVolume()`, similar to earlier commit done for another issue (Reference: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88569/files#diff-227f84916ffb93ece42ccaec840af8ea265714440c15c45f42b08d6a427a57bfR319).



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Node reboot or restart or poweroff-on scenario to be executed 

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

v1.24.7

### Cloud provider

On-premise datacenter

### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>


### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

CSI plugin: vSphere CSI driver with latest source code

@xing-yang I could test the fix locally where I check for path existence before creating the directory in kubelet and now the control gets passed to corresponding CSI driver to handle the case. Will raise PR with the changes soon.
@msau42 can you please tell whether this issue looks related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115148 or  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116618?
cc @mauriciopoppe

`It seems that Windows has a different Mount semantics, it creates the parent dir (\var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\XXXXX\) and then creates a global link there, not a directory. There are traces of this behavior in vSphere in-tree volume code:`
vSphere in-tree volume code points to NodePublishVolume() case at SetUpAt() function, not NodeStageVolume().

`It IMHO does not allow the CSI driver to replace the directory with a link, at least not in NodeStage. Just reading the spec with almost no Windows knowledge, I'd expect that drivers put a link to the device root dir into the global directory, e.g. as \var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\XXXXX\global\link. What other CSI drivers do on Windows? Shall we rephrase the spec for Windows and then fix kubelet?`
Along with vSphere CSI driver, I also checked Azure disk CSI driver and Google compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver, where in NodeStageVolume(), we expect the staging target directory (\var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\<PV/PVC ID>\globalmount) to be already created by kubelet and later it formats and **mounts** the device at the path. There is no symlink created here. Not sure if csi proxy MountVolume() method also creates symlink inside, instead of actual mount.
However, on the local setup where the issue has been reproduced, I found this pre-created staging directory has both directory and symlink mode marked.

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gcp-compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver/blob/6145c8f405d14541ae4b8923f46e3b4d072cb6a1/pkg/mount-manager/safe-mounter-v1_windows.go#L271

`Here it's pretty clear, kubelet must MkdirAll the parent dir and it already works the same on Linux and on Windows, i.e. does nothing when the directory already exists. The driver should "place the mounted directory" there, so if "mount" means "link" on Windows, then kubelet is IMO fine with that.`
Yes. For NodePublishVolume() case, in windows, we do create a symlink inside parent directory. However for parent directory, we may face the same issue if not cleaned up successfully in the volume tear down before.

@jsafrane @mauriciopoppe @msau42 another query regarding this bug - till the time this issue gets fixed, if a user comes across this scenario due to abrupt shutdown/reboot of worker node or any other case, how can one recover or workaround from this issue?

> Along with vSphere CSI driver, I also checked Azure disk CSI driver and Google compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver, where in NodeStageVolume(), we expect the staging target directory (\var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com<PV/PVC ID>\globalmount) to be already created by kubelet and later it formats and mounts the device at the path. There is no symlink created here.

Question is, what is `global/` on the filesystem. Because MkdirAll calls `IsDir()` and most probably gets `false` or error. Can you please debug where exactly MkdirAll returns error? That part should be fixed.

> > Along with vSphere CSI driver, I also checked Azure disk CSI driver and Google compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver, where in NodeStageVolume(), we expect the staging target directory (\var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com<PV/PVC ID>\globalmount) to be already created by kubelet and later it formats and mounts the device at the path. There is no symlink created here.
> 
> Question is, what is `global/` on the filesystem. Because MkdirAll calls `IsDir()` and most probably gets `false` or error. Can you please debug where exactly MkdirAll returns error? That part should be fixed.

As you suggested, I debugged further to know exact place where os.MkdirAll returns the failure and as you mentioned correctly, it failed at IsDir() call https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.21.0:src/os/path.go;drc=2291cae2af659876e93a3e1f95c708abb1475d02;l=53 since the filemode returned here is "Symbolic Link", not "Directory". Hence the function returned original error by MkDir() function, instead of succeeding for already existing directory path.
Also, as per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTFS_volume_mount_point NTFS mount points are implemented as reparse-point (similar to symlink) and do not represent actual directory. So, for windows worker nodes, in os.MkdirAll(), we should not check for presence of directory, rather a symlink. 

As you said previously, I agree that CSI spec should be reworded to consider Windows case.

Considering the mount point behavior on Windows, CSI drivers supporting windows are taking care of the symlink check correctly in IsLikelyMountPoint() function calls. Hence if kubelet checks for path already present and skips the handling to CSI drivers as done via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119735, things can work correctly.

However, what I observed on setup with issue reproduced is, "dir" command run on the corresponding windows worker node shows the staging dir path filemode as "directory + symlink". May be this could be false-positive.

`
PS C:\var\lib\kubelet\plugins\kubernetes.io\csi\csi.vsphere.vmware.com\<volumeID-hash>
8a> dir
    b1c2b36d65ba28a

Mode                LastWriteTime         Length Name
----                -------------         ------ ----
d----l        7/29/2023  11:08 PM                globalmount   <<< d=directory, l=symlink/reparse-point
-a----        7/29/2023  11:08 PM             94 vol_data.json
`

Please let me know your comments.
closing the issue as the fix done via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119735

title: Canceling the request to webhook while processing the request, webhook emits failOpen metric.
body:
### What happened?

Created a validating webhook to validate the configmap during updates. 
When tried to cancel the request while applying the update to the configmap, webhook is considering it as failOpen due to context canceled. 

### What did you expect to happen?

We expect not to consider this case as failOpen.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod with the validating webhook that validates the configmap. Set the sleep for 4 seconds before the admission response is sent by the webhook.
2. Apply the validation webhook configuration as below

```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: webhook
  namespace: kube-system
webhooks:
- name: webhook
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: $CA_BUNDLE
    url: 
  rules:
  - operations: ["UPDATE"]
    apiGroups: [ "" ]
    apiVersions: [ "v1" ]
    resources: [ "configmaps" ]
  sideEffects: None
  admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]

```

3. Then perform update to a configmap and cancel the request while processing the request i.e. before it send back the response. 
4. Check the apiserver audit logs to see the failopen due to context-canceled.

Logs: 
![Screenshot 2023-06-22 at 9 22 57 AM](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/63766150/3283bec1-3db5-4b8c-8be8-8705039ef68c)


### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

This error is not specific to k8s version but you can reproduce in 1.25

title: Authenticated field in api/authentication/v1beta1TokenReviewStatus object is omitempty when it is needed to be false
body:
### What happened?

Since the field is bool and its tag has 'omitempty', it is impossible to set it to false and perform JSON marshalling. For example, when sending [response](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#webhook-token-authentication) to KubeAPI server from a webhook-token service, if the user is not authorized, 'Authenticated' should be false, but the tag prevents serialization of the field into JSON string.



### What did you expect to happen?

Either 'omitempty' be removed or set Authenticated as *bool instead of bool

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Status := v1beta1.TokenReviewStatus{Authenticated: false, User: v1beta1.UserInfo{Username: "test"}}
StrStatus = json.Marshal(Status)
fmt.Println(StrStatus)                    // Authenticated field is omitted due to omitempty

title: kubelet without deprecated `--cloud-provider=external` do not get proper taint and are not CCM initialized
body:
### What happened?

The [kubelet CLI docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/) state that `--cloud-provider=external` is deprecated and will go away in1.24:

> 
> --cloud-provider string
> --
>  | The provider for cloud services. Set to empty string for running with no cloud provider. If set, the cloud provider > determines the name of the node (consult cloud provider documentation to determine if and how the hostname is used). (DEPRECATED: will be removed in 1.24 or later, in favor of removing cloud provider code from Kubelet.)

The [docs for running a CCM](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/running-cloud-controller/#running-cloud-controller-manager), on the other hand, say that `--cloud-provider=external` is required, in order to get the proper `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint.

I launched a single-node 1.23 cluster without `--cloud-provider=external`, and while I did not get the deprecation warnings, the node was not properly tainted, and the CCM I am running never seems to get the correct calls leading to populating the providerID and removing the taint.

I do not know if this is a bug in the controller-manager and/or kubelet, or that we need to do something else to get this to work, and thus missing documentation. 



### What did you expect to happen?

node to get the correct taint, k8s to initialize the node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Launch a single node cluster without `--cloud-provider=external`
2. See that the node does not have the taint
3. Launch a CCM
4. See that it does not set the provider ID

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

I don't think the `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint can be added to clusters without the flag passed, because that could break legitimate clusters where the flag isn't passed and a CCM isn't run.  I think the messaging is definitely confusing and we need to improve the documentation.  The `--cloud-provider=external` should probably not be deprecated, rather, the flag should specify that passing the values `aws`, .. etc are deprecated.
@nckturner Would it be a good idea to have also `--cloud-provider=none` which would make clear the taint wouldn't be applied? I guess it would also be the default.

Agreed on cases where you don't need a CCM, that it should not taint them. 

It sounds like it should not be deprecated at all, but rather should have two acceptable values:

- "none" - do not taint, no CCM expected (default)
- "external" - taint, expect CCM 


Is that it?

title: Daemonset doesn't properly respect nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.NodeSelectorTerms
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

I create `DaemonSet` in the Kubernetes v1.17.2 cluster, i use `NodeAffinity` make pods only running on the node that have specified labels, but it not work. I get the pod information and the affinity have been override.

**What you expected to happen**:

`DaemonSet` node affinity works.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. write a `DaemonSet`
2. add node affinity like below:
```yaml
affinity:
    nodeAffinity: 
        requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: 
        nodeSelectorTerms: 
        - matchExpressions: 
            - key: app
            operator: In
            values: 
            - fluent
```
3. kubectl get pod -oyaml. The pod affinity become:

```yaml
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
    - matchFields:
      - key: metadata.name
        operator: In
        values:
        - worker1
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):

`v1.17.2`

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

@dims I just experienced this behavior myself, it happens only with daemonsets where the `MatchExpressions` list inside `RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.NodeSelectorTerms[]` is overridden with:
```yaml
- matchFields:
          - key: metadata.name

```

I am not really sure whether I am missing something or node affinity does not work correctly with daemonsets.
@geokb can you check if just a regular pod works or not? (as opposed to a daemonset). please do open a fresh issue with enough info.

@dims you mean by creating a pod on its own that doesn't belong to a daemonset spec? if that's the case, at least I am certain that this behavior does not show up when using `RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.NodeSelectorTerms[].matchFields[]` with deployments, because I used this for both deployments and daemonsets. So it's obvious there is something done by some k8s master component that overrides this field in the case of daemonsets only.

/reopen
This is still an issue. The daemonset controller just straight up overrides ` nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.NodeSelectorTerms` of a pod:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7ec1e1a55e1282d791d64a8c6f874624129d2768/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L1013
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7ec1e1a55e1282d791d64a8c6f874624129d2768/pkg/controller/daemon/util/daemonset_util.go#L214-L218

The observeable behavior is that it first creates pods for nodes that have a non-matching selector but without the selector in the pod object and then later on deletes it. Depending on timing, that means that the pod might run temporarily which caused an incident for us, as it is very unexpected.

/retitle Daemonset doesn't properly respect nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.NodeSelectorTerms

nodes.body: /cc @kubernetes/sig-scheduling-bugs
To ensure spreading, you need to provide anti-affinity for your pods. Without anti-affinity, there is no guarantee that your pods will be spread among available nodes/zones/etc.
This feature predates anti-affinity?

> To ensure spreading, you need to provide anti-affinity for your pods. Without anti-affinity, there is no guarantee that your pods will be spread among available nodes/zones/etc.

Specifically, requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution if you want a guarantee. Even doing preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution isn't a guarantee.

> This feature predates anti-affinity?

Automatic best-effort spreading by set (ReplicaSet etc.) predates anti-affinity.

BTW the reason why these things aren't guaranteed is that the scheduler decides which node is best for a pod by adding up a bunch of different criteria, and spreading is just one factor, so it can be outweighed by one or more other factors (like trying to balance resource usage, trying to run on a node that already has the container image cached, etc.).
BTW the documentation on this stuff is [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/)
@craigbox Can you please let us know, if the issue still persists with pod anti-affinity with requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution flag? If not, can you close this issue?
